title: Trace Redis replication and Sentinel failover
description: Select a scenario to see which path is active, which node owns writes, and where asynchronous replication can leave a loss window.

nodes.label: Redis client
nodes.detail: Discovers the current primary through Sentinel and must reconnect after a failover. Timeouts can leave a write result ambiguous.

nodes.label: Sentinel quorum
nodes.detail: Independent Sentinel processes monitor the primary, agree on objective failure, authorize failover, and publish the new address. A robust deployment uses at least three Sentinels.

nodes.label: Primary
nodes.detail: Applies client writes and streams their effects to replicas. Replication is asynchronous by default, so an acknowledgment from this node alone is not a durable quorum commit.

nodes.label: Replica A
nodes.detail: Consumes the replication stream, tracks an offset, and may be promoted when the primary is objectively down.

nodes.label: Replica B
nodes.detail: Adds another asynchronous copy and can acknowledge received replication bytes, but it does not make Redis strongly consistent.

scenarios.label: Healthy async
scenarios.summary: The primary acknowledges a write, then sends its effects to both replicas without waiting for them.
scenarios.result: This is the normal low-latency path. A failure before a replica receives the latest bytes can lose an acknowledged write during promotion.

scenarios.label: WAIT for two
scenarios.summary: The client asks the primary to wait until two replicas acknowledge receiving the preceding writes.
scenarios.result: WAIT reduces the loss window by proving additional copies received the bytes. It does not create a strongly consistent CP system or guarantee which replica a later failover promotes.

scenarios.label: Primary fails
scenarios.summary: Sentinels agree that the primary is down, authorize a failover, and promote Replica A.
scenarios.result: Writes pause during detection and promotion. Clients must discover and reconnect to Replica A, while Replica B follows the new primary.

scenarios.label: Lagged promotion
scenarios.summary: The old primary fails after acknowledging bytes that the promoted replica has not received.
scenarios.result: The promoted replica becomes authoritative without the missing tail. Sentinel availability does not guarantee retention of every acknowledged write.

scenarios.label: No quorum
scenarios.summary: The primary is unreachable, but too few Sentinel processes can agree and authorize a safe failover.
scenarios.result: No replica is promoted, so writes remain unavailable. Placing all Sentinels in one failure domain defeats the control-plane design.
